title: Modeling the Stochastic Evolution of Predator-Prey Dynamics with Chemotaxis
content: This paper investigates a stochastic predator-prey chemotaxis system.  First, we establish the existence and uniqueness of a local mild solution using a truncation argument and the Banach fixed-point theorem. Second, we prove this solution is global almost surely using uniform a priori bounds and a blow-up criterion. Finally, we analyze how the noise intensity affects the stability of equilibria and illustrate its qualitative effects through numerical simulations. This work  provides theoretical and computational insights into the interplay between randomness and nonlinearity in prey-predator systems.
